messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user asks "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want amount of gas generated? Actually it's about expansion maybe? But they ask how much gas is generated - perhaps meaning increase in pressure or mass change? In an ideal gas scenario, no new gas produced; just same amount expands and increases pressure.

But we can compute pressure difference using PV=nRT. For constant V, P ∝ T (in Kelvin). So if initial temp 298 K, final 373K. Pressure ratio ~1.2517 times. If initial pressure 101325 Pa, final ~126700 Pa. Gas quantity remains same n=PV/RT. We could calculate moles before and after but same. Maybe answer: No additional gas generated; only increased pressure. Provide calculation.
